questions.stem: Which statement is most suitable for selecting among several constant cases?
questions.solution: switch selects a case based on a constant expression.

questions.stem: Which operator reads data from cin?
questions.solution: The extraction operator >> reads from an input stream.

questions.stem: Which values can a bool variable hold?
questions.solution: A bool holds true or false.

questions.stem: How many times does a while loop execute when its condition is false initially?
questions.solution: while is a pretest loop; a false condition skips the body.

questions.solution: Analysis establishes the requirements before design and coding.

questions.solution: break terminates the nearest loop or switch.

questions.stem: This question tests high-level languages and debugging.

parts.text: Define syntax error and logic error.
parts.answer: A syntax error violates the language grammar and is detected by the compiler. A logic error produces incorrect output although the program runs.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain TWO advantages of high-level languages over machine language.
parts.answer: They are easier to read and write, portable across machines, and supported by compilers and debugging tools.
parts.solution: Award 1.5 marks for each valid advantage.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A concert charges RM15 for ages 0-12, RM25 for ages 13-17 and RM40 for ages 18 and above. A negative age is invalid.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Start -> read age -> if age < 0 display invalid; else if age <= 12 price = 15; else if age <= 17 price = 25; else price = 40 -> display price -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, all ranges, output and flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Use if/else if with the three ranges and an invalid-age branch.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, range conditions, assignment and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests declarations, constants and expressions.

parts.text: Write C++ declarations for: an integer age, a double price, a constant discount rate of 0.10 and a character grade.
parts.answer: int age; double price; const double DISCOUNT = 0.10; char grade;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct types, names and const initialisation.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write C++ statements to read age and price, calculate price after discount, and display the result.
parts.answer: cin >> age >> price; price = price - price * DISCOUNT; cout << price;
parts.solution: Award marks for input, discount expression and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and show the exact output.
parts.solution: Award marks for each line and the exact row lengths.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Identify TWO logic errors in a version that prints four rows but reuses j without resetting it. Rewrite the corrected code.
parts.answer: The inner loop must initialise j = 1 for every row and the outer loop must run to 4. Correct code: for (int i=1;i<=4;i++){for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) cout<<j; cout<<endl;}
parts.solution: Award marks for each error and the corrected loop.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A shop stores the prices of five items in an array.

parts.text: Declare an array named prices with the values 20.5, 55.0, 15.9, 75.0 and 10.0. Display all values.
parts.answer: double prices[5] = {20.5, 55.0, 15.9, 75.0, 10.0}; for (int i=0;i<5;i++) cout << prices[i] << endl;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct type, initialiser, loop and output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment that applies a 10% discount to prices above RM50 and stores the results in a second array. Display both arrays.
parts.answer: double sale[5]; for(int i=0;i<5;i++){ sale[i] = prices[i] > 50 ? prices[i]*0.9 : prices[i]; } then display both arrays.
parts.solution: Award marks for second array, condition, discount, preservation and output.
parts.label: b
